title: 311. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Interpreting Parameters in a Quadratic Model
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Sign of the Leading Coefficient in a Quadratic Model
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the sign of \(a\) in \(y=ax^2+bx+c\) to determine the opening direction of the graph.
questions.question: In the quadratic model \(y=ax^2+bx+c\), the parameter \(a\) satisfies \(a<0\). What does this indicate about the graph?
questions.explanation: For a quadratic function \(y=ax^2+bx+c\), the sign of \(a\) determines the opening direction. If \(a>0\), the graph opens upward. If \(a<0\), the graph opens downward. Since \(a<0\), the graph opens downward.
questions.hint: Recall how the sign of the coefficient of \(x^2\) controls the direction of a parabola.

questions.concept: Meaning of Parameter \(k\) in Vertex Form
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the parameter \(k\) in \(y=a(x-h)^2+k\) as the vertical coordinate of the vertex.
questions.question: In the quadratic model \(y=a(x-h)^2+k\), what does the parameter \(k\) represent?
questions.explanation: In vertex form \(y=a(x-h)^2+k\), the vertex of the parabola is \((h,k)\). Therefore, \(h\) is the \(x\)-coordinate and \(k\) is the \(y\)-coordinate of the vertex.
questions.hint: Compare the expression with the standard vertex form and identify the coordinates of the vertex.

questions.concept: Meaning of Parameter \(h\) in Vertex Form
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the parameter \(h\) in \(y=a(x-h)^2+k\) as the horizontal coordinate of the vertex.
questions.question: In the quadratic model \(y=a(x-h)^2+k\), what does the parameter \(h\) represent?
questions.explanation: The vertex form \(y=a(x-h)^2+k\) has vertex \((h,k)\). Thus \(h\) is the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex. The \(y\)-intercept is found by substituting \(x=0\), not by reading \(h\).
questions.hint: The vertex coordinates are written directly in the form \((h,k)\).

questions.concept: Interpreting the Vertex of a Profit Model
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the vertex of a quadratic profit model to identify a maximum value.
questions.question: A profit model is \(P(x)=-2(x-10)^2+200\), where \(x\) is the number of units sold and \(P(x)\) is the profit in dollars. What does the vertex \((10,200)\) represent?

options.label: A
options.text: The minimum profit is \(200\text{ dollars}\) when \(10\) units are sold.

options.label: B
options.text: The maximum profit is \(200\text{ dollars}\) when \(10\) units are sold.

questions.explanation: The model is in vertex form with \(a=-2\). Since \(a<0\), the parabola opens downward, so the vertex gives the maximum value. The vertex is \((10,200)\), so the maximum profit is \(200\text{ dollars}\) when \(10\) units are sold.
questions.hint: Check the sign of the coefficient of the squared term to decide whether the vertex is a maximum or a minimum.

questions.concept: Meaning of the Constant Term in a Quadratic Model
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the constant term in a quadratic height model as the initial height.
questions.question: The height of a ball is modeled by \(h(t)=-5t^2+20t+1\), where \(t\) is time in seconds and \(h(t)\) is height in meters. What does the constant term \(1\) represent?

options.label: A
options.text: The initial height of the ball at \(t=0\).

options.label: B
options.text: The time when the ball reaches its maximum height.

questions.explanation: The constant term in \(h(t)=-5t^2+20t+1\) is the value of \(h(t)\) when \(t=0\). Substituting \(t=0\) gives \(h(0)=1\). Therefore, the constant term \(1\) represents the initial height of the ball.
questions.hint: Substitute \(t=0\) into the model to interpret the constant term.

questions.concept: Parameter Controlling Maximum or Minimum in Vertex Form
questions.learningObjective: Identify which parameter in \(y=a(x-h)^2+k\) determines whether the vertex is a maximum or a minimum.
questions.question: In the quadratic model \(y=a(x-h)^2+k\), which parameter determines whether the vertex is a maximum or a minimum?
questions.explanation: The sign of \(a\) determines the opening direction of the parabola. If \(a>0\), the graph opens upward and the vertex is a minimum. If \(a<0\), the graph opens downward and the vertex is a maximum. The parameter \(h\) only shifts the graph horizontally.
questions.hint: Focus on the coefficient of the squared term, not the horizontal shift.

questions.concept: Comparing Width and Direction from Parameter \(a\)
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the value of \(a\) in a quadratic model to compare width and direction with \(y=x^2\).
questions.question: The quadratic model \(y=0.5x^2-3x+4\) is compared with \(y=x^2\). Which statement correctly describes the graph?

options.label: A
options.text: It is narrower and opens downward.

options.label: B
options.text: It is wider and opens upward.

questions.explanation: The coefficient of \(x^2\) is \(0.5\). Since \(0.5>0\), the graph opens upward. Because \(|0.5|<1\), the parabola is wider than \(y=x^2\). Therefore, the correct description is wider and opening upward.
questions.hint: Use the sign of \(a\) for direction and the size of \(|a|\) for width.

questions.concept: Interpreting the Maximum Value from Vertex Form
questions.learningObjective: Determine the maximum value of a quadratic model written in vertex form.
questions.question: The model \(y=-3(x+2)^2+5\) describes a quadratic relationship. What is the maximum value of \(y\)?
questions.explanation: The equation is in vertex form \(y=a(x-h)^2+k\) with vertex \((-2,5)\). Since \(a=-3<0\), the parabola opens downward, so the vertex gives the maximum value. Therefore, the maximum value is \(5\).
questions.hint: Read the vertex from the equation, then use the sign of \(a\) to decide whether it is a maximum or a minimum.

questions.concept: Finding the Vertex from Standard Form
questions.learningObjective: Determine the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex of a quadratic model in standard form.
questions.question: The quadratic model \(P(x)=-x^2+6x-5\) has a maximum at its vertex. What is the \(x\)-coordinate of this maximum?
questions.explanation:
For \(P(x)=ax^2+bx+c\), the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is
\[
x=-\frac{b}{2a}.
\]
Here \(a=-1\) and \(b=6\), so
\[
x=-\frac{6}{2(-1)}=3.
\]
Thus the maximum occurs at \(x=3\).
questions.hint: Use the vertex formula \(x=-\frac{b}{2a}\) for a quadratic in standard form.

questions.concept: Interpreting the Horizontal Parameter in a Real-World Quadratic Model
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the parameter \(h\) in a real-world quadratic model to identify when a maximum occurs.
questions.question: A model for the height of a drone is \(y=-0.2(x-4)^2+12\), where \(x\) is time in seconds and \(y\) is height in meters. What does the parameter \(h=4\) indicate?

options.label: A
options.text: The maximum height occurs when \(x=4\text{ seconds}\).

options.label: B
options.text: The \(y\)-intercept of the graph is \(4\text{ meters}\).

questions.explanation: The model is in vertex form \(y=a(x-h)^2+k\) with \(h=4\) and \(k=12\), so the vertex is \((4,12)\). Since \(a=-0.2<0\), the graph opens downward, so the vertex gives the maximum. Therefore, the maximum height occurs when \(x=4\text{ seconds}\).
questions.hint: Identify the vertex from the equation and use the sign of \(a\) to interpret whether it is a maximum or a minimum.
